name: zvideo_fx_surface_apply_blue_tint_rect
description: zVideo_FxSurface::ApplyBlueTintRect applies the underwater blue-tint pass to the software 16-bit FX surface or queues a translucent blue quad on hardware renderer paths.
known_limits: Tier C only; no VC COFF byte-comparison target exists yet, so tier S remains open.
Binary Ninja records a known HLIL artifact for the hardware QueueSolidQuad alpha constant: assembly pushes the double 0x3fd3333333333333, i.e. 0.3, while HLIL renders the low dword as a tiny float.
functional_evidence: Binary Ninja assembly at 0x48ea20 shows ECX as an optional zVidRect32 pointer, a full-surface fallback using width - 1 and height - 1, PixelPack_GetRgbMasks output for red/green/blue masks, and a hardware path that queues a solid quad with the blue mask and alpha 0.3.

The software path widens the 16-bit RGB masks into two-pixel uint32_t masks, preserves blue bits, halves red and green bits using mask-safe right shifts, and advances by g_zVideo_FxSurfacePitchPixels16 rows.
The native zVideo smoke verifies software clipped-region tinting over two rows, untouched edge pixels, and the hardware QueueSolidQuad path's vertices and 0.3 alpha-packed blue color.
vc5_attempt: python tools/recoil.py verify vc5 --explain-missing 0x48ea20 reported no VC verification target currently covers this address.
